plot: At sunset in the park someone in the old tree copies every word Max says; Max and Mouse hunt for a twin cat, then send suspect Bird to the far side of the park, then politely try a talking tree and a big shout that only comes back louder, until Dog, who heard the tree bark back at him at the start, works out there is no copycat at all: it is an echo of their own voices, and they sing goodnight to the sun with the echo as their choir.

script.title: Who Keeps Copying Max in the Park?

beats.say: Hello, park!
And from the old tree comes a voice: 'Hello, park... park...'
Somebody is copying me! Who keeps copying me?
It is sunset in the park. The sky is pink and orange.
Max! What's wrong? You look like you swallowed a bee!
Mouse, listen. Someone in that old tree copies every word I say.
Every word? That is very rude. Or very funny.
Woof! Woof! Look, Max, I found my red ball!
Dog barks at the old tree. It barks back: 'Woof... woof...'
Ha! The tree barks just like me! Good tree!
Not now, Dog. We're solving a mystery. A copycat mystery!
We must find the copycat before the sun goes down.
Let me try a test. Hello, who are you?
The tree answers: 'Who are you... are you... you...'
It asked me back! It's a very clever copycat.
Guess one! Maybe it's another orange cat, hiding behind the tree.
A twin cat? With a red scarf, just like mine? Let's look!
Max and Mouse tiptoe around the old tree. Tiptoe, tiptoe...
...and they find one acorn, two leaves, and zero cats.
No twin cat. Just a very surprised acorn.
Hmm. Then who is talking in your voice?
Guess two! I know who loves to copy everybody. Bird!
Did someone say Bird? Here I am! Tweet, tweet!
Bird! Were you hiding in the tree, copying my words?
Me? I was busy! I was counting clouds. Fifty-two!
Fifty-two clouds? There are only three clouds in the sky!
Okay, three. But they are very, very big clouds!
That sounds like something a copycat would say.
If we don't catch the copycat soon, it will copy us forever!
Okay, Bird. Fly far away, to the other side of the park.
Fine! But I'm taking my fifty-two clouds with me!
Bird flies far, far away. Now she is a tiny dot.
Now, Copycat! Bird is gone. Say banana!
From the tree: 'Banana... nana... nana...'
It wasn't Bird! She's way over there, counting clouds!
Fifty-three! Hey, I heard that! Not me, not me!
Not a twin cat. Not Bird. Then who is it?
Guess three. Maybe the tree itself can talk!
A talking tree! Then let's be polite. Hello, Mister Tree!
'Mister Tree... Tree... Tree...' says the tree.
Mister Tree, can you say something new? Something only you know?
The tree is quiet. It says nothing new at all.
Hmm. Trees don't have mouths. So where do the words come from?
A talking tree that only says your words? That's strange.
And the sun is half gone, Max! Soon we must go home!
Let's shout really loud! Then it has to come out!
Max and Mouse take a big breath and shout: 'COME OUT!'
And the tree shouts back, louder: 'COME OUT... OUT... OUT!'
Eek! It's louder than us! And now it copies me too!
Woof! Who is shouting? I'm trying to chew my ball!
The sun is sinking low. The park is turning gold.
The sun is almost gone! We have to solve this now!
Max! Max! I know who the copycat is!
You do, Dog? Who? Tell me, quick!
It barked like me before. Now it talks like you. And Mouse.
It copies anybody who talks to the tree. So it's nobody!
Nobody? But somebody is talking! We all heard it!
Watch. The tree is hollow, like my big empty bowl.
When I bark into my bowl, the bark comes back. Woof!
'Woof... woof...' comes back from the hollow tree.
So the copycat is my own voice, bouncing back to me?
It's an echo! Your voice goes in, bounces, and comes back!
An echo? So I was right! It was not me!
Dog, you're a genius! The silliest genius in the whole park!
Let's sing goodnight to the sun. The echo can be our choir!
They sing, 'Good night, sun!' The tree sings back, 'Night... night!'
When something seems strange, listen closely. It might just be fun!
Tomorrow, let's find where Dog's ball goes under the bench!
